threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still step off the bus at the stop closest to your destination instead of walking a few minutes like everyone else.
Caught a night bus from Brixton yesterday. A guy was serenading the driver with old 90s R&B—totally made the ride feel like a reality show.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I spotted a kid riding his bike down the street, juggling oranges while his dog chased after him. Classic Neukölln chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can find public toilets with actual art inside—nothing like a mural on the wall while you do your business!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows the best taco stand changes its salsa every Sunday. Tourists grab the burritos, but we wait for the real flavor.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a guy loudly arguing about his lucky socks. He swears they’re the reason he hasn’t missed a day of work. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just for Gaudí. They miss the real charm in the tiny plazas where locals sip a café and catch up.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They stop to take photos of every single building, even the ones with graffiti. Locals just stroll past without a second glance.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stokey' instead of 'Stoke Newington' like a true local does. The subtle syntax matters here.
Last night on the 59, a guy in a suit kept shouting about how he once outran a pigeon near Windrush Square. The driver just sighed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids swapping stickers for their favorite Berliner currywurst stands at Hermannplatz. That’s when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 3 AM while a street performer raps about the night’s adventures. It's a uniquely chaotic charm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name every taco truck on 24th and still argue about their favorite burrito spot.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a Muni bus driver stopping mid-route to help an elderly lady with her groceries. Just a little kindness amidst the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but most locals just want a quiet corner café to escape the noise. The hidden gems are in the alleys.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they still use the 'Barcelona' double-decker tourist buses, despite the Metro being a few steps away.
